searchText: For one, autogen being available for just about any language out there. By contrast, I found working with existing web3 libs terrible. You can use gRPC from web browser today, there are clients out there. You can make a gRPC call directly from an address bar or browser debugger edit-and-send feature? Grpc web is still not great for production. The best way is to use a grpc gateway to transcode to a json api <@329594653097721856> Cross-language support was another big issue for Eth2 APIs. gRPC is great if you’re in Go, but the experience lessens as you diverge from langs used by Google. Rust was very average back in 2019. On the other hand, JSON parsers and HTTP impls are a likely contender for the most prolific and widely used libraries ever. You can't make POST requests from address bar either Did you use Tonic, Tokio's gRPC implementation? <@329594653097721856> we had this long discussion for eth2 and decided that grpc should be an implementation detail and not enshrined in the api standard. Since you can transcode grpc to json easily with a gateway, it becomes a client implementation choice and not a standard for everyone And that ended up being a wise decision We get to use grpc 100% while other teams can choose to do whatever suits them best, while keeping a json REST standard <@!329594653097721856> do you think you can provide the transcoder guildelines and some standardization how gRPC can coexist with JSON RPC and what the best route for existing clients and libs would be?

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
Cross-language support was another big issue for Eth2 APIs. gRPC is great if you’re in Go, but the experience lessens as you diverge from langs used by Google. Rust was very average back in 2019. 

On the other hand, JSON parsers and HTTP impls are a likely contender for the most prolific and widely used libraries ever.
